title: Asymmetric probe adaptation and token-aware autoscale safety-net
creator: Aisha Kumar
description:
Problem: We observe recurring regional autoscaler thrashing during cross-region traffic shifts where traditional readiness/liveness probes cause mass evictions or delayed failover, violating tail-latency SLOs. Root causes include noisy probe fanout, uneven token-cost per request (long generation requests consume capacity), and a lack of an admission safety-net that reasons about token budgets rather than just QPS/CPU.

Goal: Implement an asymmetric probe adaptation strategy plus a token-aware autoscale safety-net and circuit tiers to: 1) reduce probe-induced churn, 2) prioritize short/high-value requests during overload, 3) provide predictable multi-region failover behavior that keeps end-to-end SLOs intact.

High-level approach:
- Asymmetric probes: separate sampling/aggregation logic for readiness and liveness. Readiness probes will be sampled from production traffic (shadow sampling) and synthetic warmup probes, with windowing that adapts to request size distributions. Liveness probes remain fast and conservative to detect complete process loss.
- Token-aware autoscale safety-net: extend the admission controller/autoscaler input to include per-request token estimates (based on model, prompt length, and historical completion length) and maintain a token budget per pod + soft budget per region. Autoscaler uses a budgeted headroom metric in addition to CPU/GPU utilization to trigger scale-up/scale-down and to set admission limits.
- Circuit tiers and graceful load-shedding: implement tiered circuit breakers that operate on token budgets and request classes (short vs long generations, embeddings vs generation) with gradual shedding callbacks to clients (Retry-After and degraded-mode indicators) and automated fallback to lightweight model variants where configured.
- Multi-region coordination: on failover, propagate token cache/warmup signals and synthetic warm learners to the target region to reduce cold-start tail latency, while the safety-net enforces conservative admission until warm thresholds are met.

Why different from previous work: this ticket focuses on combining request cost (tokens) into the probe/autoscale decision loop and introducing asymmetric probe sampling to avoid probe storms during rapid traffic shifts. Existing tickets focused on probe smoothing and regional gating but did not integrate token-aware admission or asymmetric probe semantics.
acceptance_criteria: A1: Readiness probe sampling implemented such that only at most 10% of readiness probes fan out to downstream services in high-load scenarios (configurable), reducing probe fanout by >=70% compared to baseline.
A2: Token-aware headroom metric added to autoscaler; autoscaler must reject a scale-down if headroom < 1.25x target SLO buffer.

A3: During a simulated 40% cross-region traffic shift with mixed short/long requests, end-to-end p99 latency stays within 1.2x of baseline SLO for short requests and no more than 10% long-request failures due to admission rejection (configurable).
A4: Circuit breaker tiers can be enabled per-route, and can fall back to a configured model variant; a canary rollout enables tiered shedding in 5% increments.
A5: Observability: new dashboards showing token budget utilization, probe-sample rate, and cross-region warmup progress; alerts for safety-net engagements and unexpected probe storms.
notes: Design notes: use a separate readiness sampling service in the control plane that maintains sampling quotas per region and per-route. Readiness result aggregation will include a small decay factor for recent successful synthetic warmup hits.

Token estimation heuristics: initial estimator uses model metadata + prompt length + moving-average completion length; refine via per-route telemetry. We will expose an opt-in annotation for routes to provide custom token cost hints.

Autoscaler integration: extend existing autoscaler metrics ingestion to accept token_headroom (float) and token_utilization (percent). Scale policies evaluate both utilization and headroom. Introduce a 'safety hold' state where scaling is paused until token warm thresholds are met.

Circuit behavior: three tiers (green: full admission, amber: limited admission for long requests, red: only short/high-priority requests + fallbacks). Default policies map request classes automatically but allow route-level overrides.
Backward compatibility: defaults keep existing behavior unless route opts-in. For Dedicated customers wanting conservative behavior, enable safety-net by default behind a feature flag.
implementation_plan: Step 1 (2d): Prototype a read-only token estimator in sidecar + control-plane sampler; collect token histograms for 3 days in canary region.
Step 2 (3d): Implement asymmetric readiness sampling and control-plane quota; add probe fanout limiter and decay windowing logic.
Step 3 (3d): Add token_headroom metrics to autoscaler and implement safety hold/scale-decision hooks; unit tests for decision logic.
Step 4 (5d): Implement circuit-tier admission controller with per-route config and fallback plumbing to model variants; integrate with rollout system.
Step 5 (4d): End-to-end simulation harness (traffic generator with configurable short/long distributions) and chaos tests for region failover; iterate on policies.
Step 6 (2d): Observability and alerts, dashboard templates, and runbook updates; customer-facing docs and admin flags.
risks_and_mitigations: Risk: Token estimator mismatch causing overly conservative shedding. Mitigation: start with high headroom multiplier (2.0), short canary window, and expose opt-out per-route.

Risk: New probe sampling logic delays failover detection for full process crashes. Mitigation: keep liveness probes unchanged and ensure liveness remains high-sensitivity; readiness sampling only affects gating, not liveness-based evacuation.
Risk: Autoscaler decision complexity increases operational surprises. Mitigation: telemetry + a simulation replay mode and a 'safety hold' flag to disable token logic quickly.

Risk: Cross-region warm propagation could leak data. Mitigation: only propagate synthetic warm signals and cache metadata (no request content); follow PII rules and KMS constraints for any persisted hints.
tests_and_qa: Telemetry smoke: verify token_headroom and token_utilization metrics emitted for all pods in canary cluster.
Simulation: run 1000-run simulated failover with mixed request shapes; assert SLO windows and failure budgets.
Chaos: kill 30% of pods in origin region and trigger cross-region routing; measure p50/p95/p99 for short and long requests.
Integration: validate circuit-tier fallback by enabling red-tier for a test route and confirming traffic is admitted only for short requests and that fallback model is invoked correctly.
